questions.prompt: What is divide and conquer mainly doing in this chapter?
choices: Weakening a united opponent by widening a real internal seam
Avoiding all conflict with coalitions
Treating every member as equally movable

explanation.gentle: The chapter defines the strategy as splitting aligned actors so the pieces lose the strength of moving together.
explanation.direct: Begin with the structure: the tactic targets the coalition's alignment, not just its public argument.
explanation.competitive: Break the mass before you fight the parts.

questions.prompt: Why is a united coalition stronger than the same members standing apart?
choices: Because every coalition is morally right
Because public unity always means private agreement
Because the members lend each other cover and bargaining weight

explanation.gentle: The members add confidence, legitimacy, and cover to each other while they stay aligned.
explanation.direct: Look at the mechanism: combined action creates leverage the individual members do not have alone.
explanation.competitive: The wall hits harder than the bricks.

questions.prompt: What is the chapter's main warning about wedge work?
choices: A clumsy wedge can create stronger solidarity
Every disagreement will split a bloc instantly
The operator should always attack the loudest member first

explanation.gentle: The reversal is that bad seam work can tighten the coalition instead of weakening it.
explanation.direct: Watch the limit: a crude attempt can donate the opponent a stronger shared identity.
explanation.competitive: Miss the crack and you forge the wall harder.

questions.prompt: Aveline faces a vendor coalition blocking a data standard. What is the stronger move?
choices: Attack the entire coalition's public statement more aggressively
Press the unequal liability exposure between members
Wait for the coalition to split on its own

explanation.gentle: Aveline should work on the real burden that one member carries differently from the others.
explanation.direct: Choose the seam that changes one member's incentives instead of arguing with the whole bloc at full mass.
explanation.competitive: Go after the glue, not the speech.

questions.prompt: Maceo hears a reform bloc speak with one voice. What should he test first?
choices: Whether the bloc has a better slogan than the opposition
Whether the loudest member can speak longer
Whether the members disagree on enforcement terms

explanation.gentle: He should test the issue most likely to reveal unequal thresholds inside the bloc.
explanation.direct: Surface the enforcement split if that is where common goals stop meaning common costs.
explanation.competitive: Push the seam under the chant.

questions.prompt: Brynn finds one contract clause making a partnership unevenly costly for one partner. What fits this chapter best?
choices: Ignore the clause because public unity matters more
Press the clause if it is the real internal discomfort
Attack every partner equally so no one feels singled out

explanation.gentle: The clause matters if it is the burden one partner is carrying differently from the rest.
explanation.direct: Follow the unequal exposure rather than the polished common line.
explanation.competitive: Drive the wedge through the clause they hate carrying.

questions.prompt: Corwin accuses an entire loose group at once and the group becomes more unified. What does that show?
choices: The wedge was delicate and well aimed
The broad attack created solidarity instead of fracture
The group had no internal seams at all

explanation.gentle: The response shows that loud pressure can make loosely aligned people close ranks.
explanation.direct: This is the classic failure mode: collective attack creates a stronger common identity.
explanation.competitive: He hit wide and welded them tighter.

questions.prompt: Ilaria has time to press one issue inside a reform bloc. Which choice best fits divide and conquer?
choices: Press the enforcement issue that members cannot absorb equally
Attack the most dramatic public sentence
Spread mild pressure across every issue at once

explanation.gentle: She should choose the issue that exposes unequal burden inside the bloc.
explanation.direct: Select the seam that changes one member's calculation, not the loudest talking point.
explanation.competitive: Hit the crack, not the poster line.

questions.prompt: What is the ethical limit on this strategy in the chapter?
choices: The operator should invent conflict whenever a coalition is inconvenient
The operator may widen an existing real seam, but fabricating conflict turns the move dirty
Any split is justified if it produces speed

explanation.gentle: The line is crossed when the operator manufactures conflict instead of working on a real mismatch.
explanation.direct: Keep the distinction clear: widening an existing seam differs from planting a false one.
explanation.competitive: Use the crack that exists, do not counterfeit one.

questions.prompt: After fragmenting a coalition in Chapter 17, what strategic move comes next in Chapter 18?
choices: Return to a frontal clash with the strongest side
Keep every member equally active forever
Attack the soft flank instead of the strong front

explanation.gentle: The next chapter stays indirect and turns from coalition seams to weak-side attack.
explanation.direct: Move from wedge work to the soft flank.
explanation.competitive: After the split, hit the weak side.
